# ProgressBar

<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-component-docs.mjs from ai/component-catalog.json and ai/component-composition.json. Do not edit; run `npm run catalog:sync`. -->

`@kerfjs/ui:progress-bar` · Kerf UI · component · Feedback

A linear progress indicator on the native progress element: determinate value of max or an indeterminate sweep, a visible label or ariaLabel, an optional value or valueText readout, brand or status tones, and a default or compact track.

## When to use

Show how far a measurable task has gone (an upload, a migration, a quota) or that work of unknown size is under way.

- A task reports measurable progress (files uploaded, steps completed, quota used): pass value and max, a label, and showValue or valueText for the readout.
- Work of unknown length is under way and a full-width indicator fits: omit value for the indeterminate sweep.

**Not when:**

- Do not use it for a small inline busy state; use LoadingSpinner or an indeterminate ProgressRing.
- Do not use it for a scale reading that is not progress (a rating, a level); use a native meter.
- Do not use wa-progress-bar.

**Alternatives:**

- [ProgressRing](./progress-ring.md) (nearest) — Use a ProgressRing where a bar does not fit, inline in a row or toolbar.
- [LoadingSpinner](./loading-spinner.md) (nearest) — Use a LoadingSpinner for a brief busy state with no measurable progress.

## Imports

- JavaScript: `@kerfjs/ui/progress-bar` — exports `ProgressBar`, `ProgressBarProps`, `ProgressBarSize`, `ProgressBarRootAttributes`, `ProgressTone`.
- CSS: the browser build of `@kerfjs/ui/progress-bar` pulls its CSS automatically; import `@kerfjs/ui/progress-bar.css` manually only without the `browser` export condition.
- Declared side effects: browser-condition-css.

## Props

Exact prop names and types: [`@kerfjs/ui/progress-bar`](../public-api-signatures-v1.md#kerfjsuiprogress-bar) in `public-api-signatures-v1.md`. Do not infer props from examples.

**Variants (configure, do not restyle):**

- determinate with a label and value readout
- indeterminate sweep
- brand, success, warning, or danger tone
- default 6px or compact 4px track
- ariaLabel without a visible label

## Composition

- Parents: any.
- Contexts: `application-ui`.
- Children: unrestricted.

## State and wiring

**The app owns:** the value, max, and valueText; the label or ariaLabel; the tone and size.

No wiring helper.

## Geometry

Margin: none · border: self · padding: self (layout role: feedback). `self` means the component already owns it — do not add wrapper padding, margin, or borders around it.

- It fills the available width with the shared block-content inset (a transparent 1px border and 8px padding); the label row sits 4px above the track.

## Accessibility

- The native progress element is the progressbar: a visible label names it through aria-labelledby (or ariaLabel without one), and valueText replaces the spoken percentage.
- The indeterminate sweep holds still under prefers-reduced-motion or the static-effects switch; forced colors draw a CanvasText-bordered track with a Highlight fill.

## Styling boundary

The component owns its own styles. Configure it through its props and variants; do not override its internals.

Public class hooks (select for layout placement only, never to change the component's look): `kui-progress-bar`, `kui-progress-bar__header`, `kui-progress-bar__label`, `kui-progress-bar__value`, `kui-progress-bar__track`.

Never put `kui-progress-bar`, `kui-progress-bar__header`, `kui-progress-bar__label`, `kui-progress-bar__value`, `kui-progress-bar__track` on an element you write; render `ProgressBar` instead (`KUI-L103`).

Everything else is internal: `kerf-ui-analyze` reports private or unknown `.kui-*` selectors (`KUI-L001`, `KUI-L010`), unknown or private tokens (`KUI-L002`, `KUI-L012`), and any application rule that restyles the component, forced dimensions included (`KUI-L019`).
